rows.source_excerpt: Larger pipe sizes, such as the 3-inch trap arm minimum for a toilet, are typically restricted to a maximum length of 6 feet (72 inches) under the UPC.
rows._note: 6 feet = 1.8288m; rounded to 1.83m. WC minimum drain 3 inch = 76mm but Indian practice typically uses 100mm. Pending primary-source verification for India-specific applicability.

rows.source: IPC Table 909.1 (1-1/4 inch trap = 30 inches max)
rows._note: 30 inches = 0.762m; the 1.07m figure assumes 1-1/2 inch trap (42 inches = 1.07m) which is more common in modern lavatories. Verification pending.
60 inches = 1.524m → rounded to 1.52m. Indian shower stalls vary; verify against state-specific practice.
Bathtubs less common in Indian residential v1 scope; included for completeness.
42 inches = 1.067m → 1.07m. NSPC DFU = 2 for kitchen sink.
Utility-room laundry/washing sink. Similar profile to kitchen sink.
Floor drain DFU = 0 per NSPC Table 11.4.1 but trap-arm constraint still applies. Indian bathroom floor drains are universal but not covered cleanly in IPC primary source.

_global_constants.max_slope_source: one pipe diameter per foot (UPC max — beyond this, velocity strips water from pipe walls and induces siphon)
_global_constants._note: Slope feasibility check is C12/C14 territory; C10 only emits horizontal run distances and trap arm distances. Slopes recorded here as forward-compat KB anchor.
